answers.answer: They cannot win immediately when taking Oathkeeper during Act. At their next Wake, the Usurper victory check happens before an Exile holding Oathkeeper flips the title to Usurper, so they still do not win then. They can first win at the following Wake, when still an Exile Usurper, or at the end of round 8 if that occurs first while they remain Usurper. If they lose the title, the Usurper win is prevented; retaking it resets it to Oathkeeper and restarts the sequence.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions, Usurper victory: ‘next Wake check (not yet Usurper), then flip to Usurper, then win at the following Wake or at the end of round 8’; losing title prevents win and retaking resets it.

answers.answer: Supremacy matches Conquest; People matches Rebellion; Protection matches Sanctuary; Devotion matches Faith. A Visionary win also requires an Exile to have the true Vision revealed and its goal complete at Wake, plus at least 3 Visions drawn from the world deck by all players combined. For Conquest and Sanctuary, ‘most’ means strictly more than every other player; a tie does not count.
answers.evidence: Oath/Vision table and Visionary victory paragraph: at least 3 world-deck Visions globally; Conquest/Sanctuary require strictly more, no ties.

answers.answer: At the ends of rounds 5, 6, and 7, roll the end die only if the Chancellor or a Citizen is Oathkeeper. The game ends on a 6 in round 5, 5–6 in round 6, or 3–6 in round 7. An Exile Oathkeeper or Usurper prevents the roll.
answers.evidence: Stable regime: ends of rounds 5/6/7, results 6 / 5–6 / 3–6; Exile Oathkeeper/Usurper prevents the roll.

answers.answer: Round 8 ends automatically. Check in order: (1) if Chancellor or Citizen is Oathkeeper, Empire wins—Chancellor unless a Citizen qualifies as Successor; (2) otherwise an Exile Usurper wins; (3) otherwise a qualifying revealed Exile Vision wins, with simultaneous qualifying Visions prioritized Conquest, Rebellion, Sanctuary, Faith; (4) otherwise Empire wins, again Chancellor unless a qualified Successor replaces them. A Citizen Successor wins alone instead of the Chancellor whenever the Chancellor would win. A mere Exile Oathkeeper does not prevent the final Empire fallback.
answers.evidence: War exhaustion lists the four priorities; it states Successor replaces any Chancellor win and Empire fallback applies even if an Exile is only Oathkeeper.

answers.answer: Supremacy: hold more relics and banners than the Chancellor and every other Citizen. People: hold Darkest Secret. Protection: hold People's Favor. Devotion: hold Grand Scepter. Citizens and the Chancellor cannot win by true Vision or Usurper; holding a Successor goal does not end the game by itself and only replaces a Chancellor win.
answers.evidence: Oath table gives the four Citizen Successor goals; Visionary paragraph excludes Citizens/Chancellor from Vision and Usurper wins; war exhaustion says Successor goal alone never ends game.

answers.answer: At Wake, if you hold People's Favor, choose to put 1 favor from your board onto it or return 1 favor from it to a least-full suit bank, choosing among tied least-full banks. Never remove its last favor: if it has 1, you must add a favor if able; if you have none, nothing happens. If it is already Mob-side, repeat this choice once. After the choice(s), check whether it has 6 or more favor and flip it to Mob. Becoming Mob at that final check does not cause an extra payment/repetition that Wake.
answers.evidence: Wake step 1: choice, preserve last favor, repeat if already Mob, then check 6+ and flip; no retroactive repeat if it flips at the last step.

answers.answer: Rest order: (1) return favor on denizens/edifices to suit-matching banks; (2) return secrets on denizens/edifices/relics to your board and flip facedown secrets on your board faceup; (3) refresh Supply—Exile/Chancellor according to warbands remaining in personal bank, while a Citizen uses the exact Chancellor marker space, including the leftmost space, rather than counting purple warbands; (4) save unspent Supply by moving the marker one extra space left per unspent Supply, capped at the leftmost (7 Supply); (5) optional Rest powers, each once, in chosen order. Chancellor gets 6/5/4/3 Supply for 18+/11–17/4–10/0–3 bank warbands; Exile gets 6/5/4 for 9+/4–8/0–3.
answers.evidence: Rest mandatory order steps 1–5 and the Chancellor/Exile refresh thresholds; Citizen refreshes to exact Chancellor marker space; save remaining Supply capped leftmost.

answers.answer: Search costs 2–4 Supply and chooses either the world deck or the discard pile for your pawn's region, never both. Discard-pile Search costs 2. World-deck Search costs 2 at 0 Visions drawn, 3 at 1–2, and 4 at 3–5; Darkest Secret changes the world-deck cost to 2, with other modifiers still applying. Draw 3 unless the source runs out, a world-deck Vision stops you, or a modifier reduces the draw; you cannot voluntarily stop early. Draw from the world deck one at a time; when a Vision appears, announce that a Vision was drawn, stop immediately, and advance Visions Drawn by 1. A Vision drawn from a discard pile does not stop the draw or advance the track. No reshuffle is implied when the source runs out.
answers.evidence: Search section gives source/cost table, Darkest Secret adjustment, draw limits, and distinct world-deck versus discard Vision behavior.

answers.answer: Put discarded cards facedown atop the next region's pile in the cycle Cradle → Provinces → Hinterland → Cradle; choose the order for multiple cards and never use the same-region pile. Cards from hand/advisers use the pile determined by your pawn's region: Cradle to Provinces, Provinces to Hinterland, Hinterland to Cradle. When discarding a card from a site in another region, use that card's region for the cycle rather than your pawn's. Any favor on a discarded card immediately returns to its matching bank; secrets go to the acting player's board facedown.
answers.evidence: Discard destinations paragraph specifies regional cycle, remote-site exception, and disposition of favor and secrets.

answers.answer: You may have up to 3 advisers total, counting faceup and facedown; before exceeding the limit, discard an adviser subject to locks. If the incoming card changes the limit, apply the new limit before playing it; with multiple limits, use the lowest. A facedown adviser has no suit, restriction banner, or power, and any card—including site-only cards and Visions—may be held facedown. Later, as a minor action, play a facedown adviser faceup to a legal destination or discard it. You cannot discard a faceup adviser at will; it can be discarded only when another rule permits or requires it. An Exile may reveal a true Vision faceup in the separate Revealed Vision space, replacing and discarding their old revealed Vision; it is not an adviser. Chancellor/Citizens may hold true Visions facedown but cannot reveal them.
answers.evidence: Search adviser and true Vision options specify the 3-card limit, facedown properties/later options, and Exile-only Vision reveal/replacement.

answers.answer: Both Muster and Trade cost 1 Supply. Muster: at your pawn's site, put 1 favor on an empty denizen or intact edifice (no favor or secrets already), then gain 2 warbands from your personal bank onto your board; Citizens gain purple. Relics and ruins are ineligible; rule is not required, but ruling a remote site does not permit remote Muster. Trade uses an empty denizen or intact edifice at your pawn's site (not relics or ruins). Either put 1 secret on it to gain 1 favor plus 1 per matching faceup adviser from that card's suit bank, or put 2 favor on it to gain 1 shared-bank secret per matching faceup adviser. Facedown advisers never match. With no matching adviser, the second Trade yields zero secrets, though the 2-favor cost remains. Favor/warbands are limited by available supply; secrets are unlimited.
answers.evidence: Muster and Trade sections give costs, eligible card condition/location, gains, matching rules, and finite-source limitation.

answers.answer: Recover costs 1 Supply plus the target's cost. A relic must be facedown at your site; pay its printed site cost (3 favor to the indicated bank, burn 2 favor, burn 1 secret, or burn 2 secrets) and take it faceup into your personal bank. A banner may be recovered from anywhere, including yourself or the shared bank. For People's Favor, pay strictly more favor than it currently has, place the payment on it, distribute its old favor one token at a time among suit banks starting at a chosen bank and proceeding through the printed bank order, and flip it to normal if Mob; the old favor does not go to the previous holder and there is no seizure penalty. For Darkest Secret, pay strictly more secrets than it holds; put the payment on it, the new holder takes 1 old secret and the previous holder takes the rest. If recovering it from yourself, all old secrets return to you; from the shared bank, the remainder stays there. Player-held or Reliquary relics cannot be recovered.
answers.evidence: Recover section states 1 Supply, relic eligibility/costs, both banner payment rules, old-resource destinations, and unavailable relics.

answers.answer: To recover Darkest Secret from another player, there must be a suited card at their pawn's site whose suit matches none of that player's faceup advisers. Thus an empty site or a ruin-only site protects it because there is no suited card. If the holder has no faceup advisers but the site has a suited card, it is recoverable because that card matches none of their advisers. Ruins and facedown advisers have no suit. This protection does not apply when recovering from yourself or the shared bank.
answers.evidence: Corrected Darkest Secret protection rule states the suited-card/no-matching-adviser condition and specifically explains empty, ruin-only, and no-adviser cases.

answers.answer: For 2 Supply, choose any other player who rules your site or whose pawn is there. If no player rules your site, you may choose bandits. At least one declared target must be at your pawn's site; if the defender rules that site, you must target it. You may additionally target any of the defender's sites anywhere on the map, each adding 1 defense die. If the defender's pawn is at your site, you may also target any of their relics (their printed defense dice), banners (dice equal to resources on the banner), or their pawn and favor together (2 dice). A co-located defender's relic target satisfies the local-target requirement.
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 1–2 specify eligible defender, local target requirement, mandatory ruled local site, remote sites and co-located relic/banner/pawn targets.

answers.answer: The attacker chooses up to as many attack dice as there are warbands in the attacking force, then applies relevant modifiers. Defense is shields rolled, doubled for each double-symbol (multipliers stack), plus all defending warbands at targeted sites, plus the defender's board force if their pawn is at the attacker's site or a targeted site; doubles multiply shields only, not warbands. Bandits add 1 per targeted bandit site. Each attack skull immediately kills one of the attacker's force warbands. Count full swords; each pair of hollow swords adds 1 attack and an unpaired hollow sword adds zero. The attacker may sacrifice surviving force warbands for +1 attack each, but if sacrificing, must sacrifice exactly enough to win and never excess. Attack must strictly exceed defense; a tie is a defender win. The Oathkeeper adds 1 mandatory defense die and Usurper adds 2.
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 2, 4–5 give dice, defense formula, skull/sword/sacrifice rules and strict-win threshold; title defense bonus is specified in step 2.

answers.answer: On attacker victory, first the defender kills half the warbands in its defending force, rounded down, and returns the rest to board; resolve defeated-plan effects. Then the attacker may place any number—including zero—of surviving force warbands on any targeted sites. Zero leaves a site to bandits unless another power applies. The attacker takes all targeted relics and banners. A banner seized by Campaign (unlike Recover) loses 2 resources, down to a minimum of 1, and People's Favor flips to Mob. If pawn-and-favor was targeted, the attacker may force the defender to travel to a legal chosen site for no Supply and may independently burn half the defender's board favor, rounded down. Respect travel restrictions; Shrouded Wood can override who chooses the destination. Finally resolve the attacker's victorious plan effects and any end-discard plan effects. If defender wins, attacker loses half its remaining force rounded down, attacker targets are skipped, and defender victorious effects resolve.
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 6–8 order defeat/casualties before targets, allow zero garrisons, state banner penalty and banishment effects, and finish battle plans.

answers.answer: When an Imperial player defends, Chancellor automatically joins as Ally; other non-attacking Citizens may join with the defender's permission if their pawn is at the attacker's site or a targeted site. Activate all Campaign modifiers ruled by defender/Allies and share side powers: ‘you,’ ‘your enemy,’ and ‘defender’ refer to the defending side, while ‘your site’/‘your board’ still refer to each user's own. Allied board warbands add defense only if their pawn is at the attacker site or a targeted site. Defenders/Allies may use plans at Imperial sites and their own advisers, not other players' advisers; the user of a plan pays its cost, and a plan is used by only one player. The declared defender resolves disagreements over order/timing/priority. Chancellor chooses Imperial defending casualties; surviving site garrisons go to Chancellor's board, while surviving warbands on Citizens' boards stay there. An intra-Empire Campaign does not make every Citizen non-Imperial. A Citizen who attacks Chancellor or another Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign; when Chancellor attacks a Citizen, that Citizen is non-Imperial for it.
answers.evidence: Imperial defense bullets state ally permissions, modifiers/shared powers, force and plan access/cost, casualty handling, and limited status exception; Campaign step 1 states Citizen attacker exceptions.

answers.answer: Travel costs 1–4 Supply before modifiers. Base cost by origin→destination region: Cradle→Cradle 1, Provinces 2, Hinterland 4; Provinces→Cradle/Provinces/Hinterland 2 each; Hinterland→Cradle 4, Provinces 2, Hinterland 3. Move to any different site, not necessarily adjacent. If the destination is facedown, reveal it and place its printed favor/secrets from the shared bank and printed number of relics from the relic deck facedown beside it. Pay the fixed-number cost first, then apply other increases/decreases. Any applicable free-Travel power is the final override that makes the Supply payment zero despite increases. Site-entry restrictions still apply unless ignored by a rule/power. Examples of modifiers in the summary: Coast-to-Coast costs 1 and ignores Narrow Pass; Charming Valley increases cost by 1; Shrouded Wood travel from it costs 2; Decadent makes Provinces/Hinterland-to-Cradle free but increases Travel to Hinterland by 1; Buried Giant can make Travel free by flipping a board secret facedown and ignoring Narrow Pass.
answers.evidence: Travel table and paragraph define base costs, reveal stocking, modifier order/free override and restrictions; Site Reference and Decadent list examples.

answers.answer: The Grand Scepter holder, including an Exile, may offer Citizenship to any Exile, including themself, but cannot use the Scepter's powers on the turn they took it and cannot offer that turn. A later offer must promise exactly one Reliquary relic; the parties may also negotiate binding exchanges of favor, secrets, banners, and non-Reliquary relics, and the recipient may be allowed to peek at Reliquary relics. On acceptance, the recipient flips to Citizen, replaces all own board and map warbands with purple (if purple pieces are insufficient, the new Citizen chooses which to remove/replace), discards any revealed Vision, flips Usurper title to Oathkeeper, ends their Act if it is their turn, and refreshes to full leftmost Supply. Exchange promised pieces, and Chancellor takes the newly uncovered mandatory Reliquary modifier. Forced-Citizenship powers use the same status-conversion steps but do not require a Scepter offer, relic gift, or invented exchange; a modifier is uncovered only when a Reliquary relic is actually removed.
answers.evidence: Citizenship and exile section specifies timing/eligibility, required and optional offer terms, acceptance effects, and forced-Citizenship exception.

answers.answer: For the next Chronicle Oath, if the winner won solely by Vision, use the Oath matching that Vision; for any other or multiple victory method, choose any Oath except the current one and save its goal. For free Chronicle Citizenship, if the winner is an Exile, flip all Citizen boards (including boxed ones) to Exile, then the winner may offer Citizenship to other Exiles except those just flipped; each accepting Exile flips to Citizen and replaces every garrison at every site they rule with exactly one winner-color warband. The winner cannot offer to themself. Rebuild the world deck from denizens remaining in play: top stack is 10 denizens plus 2 random Visions (12 cards); middle is 15 denizens plus remaining 3 Visions (18 cards); remaining denizens go below. The aid's ‘12 denizens + 2’ instruction is incorrect; 12 denizens plus 2 Visions would be 14, but the summary specifies 10 denizens plus 2 Visions.
answers.evidence: Chronicle steps 1–2 give Oath and Citizenship turnover; step 9 explicitly sets 10 denizens + 2 Visions = 12 and corrects the aid's 12 + 2 error.
